topic: the US military intervention in the Russian Civil War, Kolchak's betrayal, and the Czechoslovak Legion mutiny
title: The US Invaded Russia In 1918 And Almost Nobody Remembers
description: AI-narrated commentary on the forgotten Allied intervention in the Russian Civil War: American troops fighting Bolshevik forces, the betrayal of Admiral Kolchak, and the mutiny that dragged Siberia into war.

hook_candidates.text: Facts about America's secret war in Russia that sound made up.
The US Army invaded Russia in 1918, and almost nobody remembers it.
You think the Cold War was the first US-Russia fight. It wasn't.
Did you know American troops fought Soviet Russia a year after World War One ended?

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists the Cold War started the rivalry, because they want to prove American and Russian troops fought decades earlier.
contradicted_belief: Most people have never heard about the secret war America fought against Russia in 1918.
closing_comment: That typhus death toll is wild. More people died from disease in the Russian Civil War than in combat itself.

sources.note: About 13,000 US troops fought Bolshevik forces in North Russia and Siberia, 1918-1920.
Czechoslovak Legion handed Admiral Kolchak to Bolsheviks for safe rail passage; he was executed.
Confirms Russian Civil War death toll dominated by disease and famine, not combat.
50,000-strong Czechoslovak Legion revolted after a weapons dispute, seizing the Trans-Siberian Railway.
